evidence.title: Patient choice before follow-up booking
evidence.need: The trust describes a choice-booking pilot covering over 2,000 follow-up appointments in five services: a text to confirm need, telephone offers closer to the appointment, and a letter if contact fails.
evidence.context: This was a follow-up pilot, not the first-appointment population in the default HES view. Reported local improvements must not be used as assumed JUNO effects.

route.label: Paddington Life Sciences — commercial partnerships
route.text: The official NHS partnership site lists Dr Suki Balendra for commercial partnership enquiries.

evidence.question: Which first-appointment or exception-handling workflows remain outside the choice-booking process, and what would a complementary pilot measure?
evidence.incumbent: An established choice-booking pilot covers follow-up appointments. This is a workflow comparator, not proof of unmet first-appointment demand.

evidence.title: Booking-rule alignment and outpatient access
evidence.need: The trust says dermatology improved booking processes and aligned booking rules, creating more than 150 additional new outpatient appointments per month with benefits expected from June.
evidence.context: A dermatology improvement example, not evidence that all trust-level first cancellations originate in dermatology or that those processes remain manual.

route.label: Research and Innovation — Industry and Contracts team

route.caveat: Research/industry entry point, not evidence of purchasing authority for outpatient operations.

evidence.question: Which queues still require manual coordination after booking-rule alignment and app rollout, and which service owner could sponsor a measured workflow pilot?
evidence.incumbent: Booking rules have already been improved. The trust also announced an app for booking and rescheduling. Confirm what has been implemented and where staff still need to coordinate tasks.

evidence.title: Fragmented booking administration and patient contact
evidence.need: The trust describes its April 2026 Patient Services Hub replacing fragmented administration across 15 systems and 40 mailboxes. It says three-quarters of prior calls concerned checking, rebooking or cancelling appointments.
evidence.context: The same update reports automated self-service, SMS filling of short-notice slots and a six-month implementation pause announced in July. This is an active programme with implementation concerns, not evidence of available procurement.

route.label: Research and Innovation enquiries
route.caveat: A general research route only; a specific outpatient innovation or purchasing route was not verified.

evidence.question: After the Patient Services Hub review, which exceptions still need staff coordination, and is a complementary measured pilot appropriate before further rollout?
evidence.incumbent: The Patient Services Hub already offers booking automation. The trust reports a six-month rollout pause announced in July 2026. Establish the current programme status before proposing anything.

evidence.title: Late rebooking communication and administrative capacity
evidence.need: The outpatient DNA section reports PAS-to-Accurx feed problems, late cancellation/rebooking letters and limited administrative capacity to answer calls or action cancel/rebook requests. It also states that Accurx reminders are live in most services.
evidence.context: This is a reported outpatient DNA root-cause analysis, not an explanation of all hospital-cancelled first appointments in HES.

route.label: Health Innovation Hub — industry solution submission
route.text: Official innovation front door welcomes industry proposals and supports pilots, implementation and scale.

evidence.question: Which cancellation/rebooking queues remain manual after Accurx/PAS work, OTTO and imaging automation, and can we measure the remaining staff handling time?
evidence.incumbent: Accurx reminders are live in most services. OTUA is named in the NHS plan; its supplier reports an OTTO rollout. A separate Dedalus award covers imaging booking automation. Check remaining manual queues with each system owner.
